title: GitHub Actions
concept: Set up GitHub Actions workflows for XIOM projects — automated testing, multi-platform builds, and deployment on every push.
why: GitHub Actions is the most-used CI platform. Setting it up correctly gives you free, automated quality checks on every commit — no server maintenance needed.
theory:
## Complete XIOM CI Workflow

### Basic CI Workflow

```yaml
# .github/workflows/ci.yml
name: XIOM CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  quality:
    name: Code Quality
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Setup XIOM
        uses: xiom-lang/setup-xiom@v1
        with:
          xiom-version: stable

      - name: Cache dependencies
        uses: actions/cache@v3
        with:
          path: ~/.xiom/cache
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-xiom-${{ hashFiles('**/package.xi') }}

      - name: Check formatting
        run: xiom fmt --check src/

      - name: Lint
        run: xiom lint --deny-warnings src/

      - name: Run tests
        run: xiom test --verbose

      - name: Build release
        run: xiom build --release
```

### Multi-Platform Matrix Build

```yaml
jobs:
  build:
    name: Build (${{ matrix.os }})
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    strategy:
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest, windows-latest]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: xiom-lang/setup-xiom@v1
      - run: xiom build --release
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3
        with:
          name: binary-${{ matrix.os }}
          path: target/release/myapp
```

### Release Workflow

```yaml
on:
  push:
    tags: ['v*']

jobs:
  release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: xiom-lang/setup-xiom@v1
      - run: xiom build --release
      - name: Create Release
        uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v1
        with:
          files: target/release/*
```

tips: Use `actions/cache` for XIOM dependencies — dramatically speeds up CI
Matrix builds catch platform-specific bugs early — test on all target OSes
Use `xiom-lang/setup-xiom` action — it handles toolchain installation automatically
Add contract verification to CI if you use contracts — catches regressions before merge
common_mistakes: Not caching dependencies — slow CI discourages frequent commits
Using `ubuntu-latest` for everything — test on your actual target platform
Forgetting to add contract verification to CI — contracts aren't checked at runtime in release
